title: Vertex Form by Completing the Square

steps.body: You've read vertices FROM vertex form — now derive it. For y = x² − 6x + 5, add and subtract (6/2)² = 9 **on the same side**: y = (x² − 6x + 9) − 9 + 5 = **(x − 3)² − 4**. Add-and-subtract keeps y unchanged — there's no other side to balance on.
Completing the square IS finding the vertex.

widget.prompt: x² − 6x + 5 completes to (x − 3)² − 4. Build it, and see what the completed form was hiding.
widget.successFeedback: Vertex (3, −4). Standard form buries the vertex; vertex form hands it to you. Completing the square is not an algebraic ritual — it is the change of address that makes the vertex readable.
widget.shapeFeedback: The shape is a = 1 here — only the vertex needs moving.
widget.vertexFeedback: (x − 3)² − 4 has its vertex at (3, −4): right 3, down 4.

predict.prompt: You'll move h UP in y = a(x − h)² + k. Which way does the parabola slide?
predict.reveal: Raising h moves the vertex RIGHT even though h is subtracted — (x − h)² is smallest exactly when x = h, so the low point chases h. The minus sign is why so many people guess the wrong direction.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents cts vertex.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for cts vertex must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines cts vertex.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: Why it's legal: +9 − 9 = 0, so y never changed — it just regrouped. The payoff is instant: (x − 3)² − 4 hands you the vertex **(3, −4)** and the minimum value −4 with no formula at all.

widget.prompt: What is the vertex form of y = x² + 4x + 1?

options.label: y = (x + 2)² + 1
options.feedback: The +4 tucked into the square must be paid back — subtract 4 from the 1: constant −3.

options.label: y = (x + 2)² + 5
options.feedback: That's 1 + 4 — the compensation SUBTRACTS the added 4: 1 − 4 = −3.

options.label: y = (x − 2)² − 3
options.feedback: Half of +4 is +2, so the square is (x + 2)² — the inside sign matches b's sign.

widget.prompt: y = x² + 10x + 30 becomes (x + 5)² + k. What is k?

commonErrors.feedback: 30 is the original constant — pay back the 25 hidden in the square: 30 − 25 = 5.

explanationVariants: y = (x − 4)² − 13, so the vertex y-coordinate is −13.
(−8/2)² = 16; the constant becomes 3 − 16 = −13, which is the minimum value.

widget.prompt: Convert y = x² − 8x + 3 to vertex form. What is the y-coordinate of the vertex?

commonErrors.feedback: 3 is the y-INTERCEPT (the value at x = 0) — the vertex height is 3 − 16 = −13.
That's 3 + 16 — the 16 slipped into the square is paid back by SUBTRACTING: −13.

widget.fallbackFeedback: y = (x − 4)² − 13; vertex height −13. Check: at x = 4, 16 − 32 + 3 = −13. ✓

explanationVariants: y = x² − 2x + 7 = (x − 1)² + 6, so the vertex is (1, 6).
Add-and-subtract 1: constant 7 − 1 = 6; the square puts x = 1.

widget.prompt: After completing the square on y = x² − 2x + 7, what is the vertex?

options.feedback: The square is (x − 1)², and (x − h)² puts the vertex at x = +1, not −1.
7 hasn't paid back the +1 tucked into the square: 7 − 1 = 6.
(0, 7) is the y-INTERCEPT — the vertex sits on the axis of symmetry at x = 1.

explanationVariants: y = (x + 6)² + 4, so the minimum value is 4 (reached at x = −6).
(12/2)² = 36; constant 40 − 36 = 4 — an upward parabola's vertex height IS its minimum.

widget.prompt: What is the MINIMUM value of y = x² + 12x + 40?

commonErrors.feedback: 40 is the y-intercept — pay back the 36 hidden in (x + 6)²: 40 − 36 = 4.

widget.fallbackFeedback: y = (x + 6)² + 4; the square is never negative, so the minimum is 4. Check x = −6: 36 − 72 + 40 = 4. ✓

hints: Complete the square: half of 12 is 6, squared is 36.
The squared part bottoms out at 0, so the minimum is 40 − 36 = 4.

steps.body: Add-and-subtract (b/2)² on one side to regroup y into vertex form.
takeaways: On an expression (not an equation), compensate on the SAME side: +9 − 9.
Vertex form hands you the vertex and the max/min instantly.
The y-intercept (x = 0 value) is NOT the vertex height.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: the number that finally solves x² = −1.

concept.body: Small version: y = x² + 2x + 5. Add and subtract (2/2)² = 1: y = (x + 1)² + (5 − 1).

explanationVariants: The +1 inside the square is paid back by subtracting 1 from the 5.

widget.prompt: y = x² + 2x + 5 becomes (x + 1)² + k. What is k?

commonErrors.feedback: 5 still owes the +1 tucked into the square: 5 − 1 = 4.
